analytic.title: Fast Responsive Framework for Optimal Power Flow Analysis in Power System

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: The analysis of optimal power flow (OPF) plays an important role in the safe operation, economic dispatching and reliability analysis in modern power system. However, with the large-scale integration of renewable energy sources and power electronics, higher requirements are put forward for online analysis of power system. Most previous studies only focused on the execution efficiency of the algorithm without considering the cost of data processing and transmission. In fact, the transmission of massive data between different platforms and computational nodes is the major factor limiting the response time of online analysis. In this paper, a fast responsive framework, which integrates the in-memory data grid and parallel computing, is proposed to improve the response time of OPF analysis. The case studies based on the IEEE baseline network show that the proposed framework can greatly improve the speed of data access and accelerate the computing time of OPF.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Optimal power flow (OPF) refers to the optimization process in which the various control parameters are adjusted under the constraints of power balance and safe operation. It plays an important role in maintaining the safety and economic operation of power system. Therefore, how to improve the real-time analysis ability of power system has become a research hotspot in academics and industry.

As shown in Fig. 1, the previous work of OPF analysis can be generally divided into two parts. One is focused on the algorithm improvement, which can be specified in three aspects: the conventional methods, the distributed approaches and the introduction of artificial intelligence theory. Among the conventional methods, the interior-point method [1] and Newton's method [2] are widely used, both of which are optimized solutions based on derivatives. Mehrtash et al. [3] proposed a partition-based bus renumbering algorithm from the perspective of power system modeling. By constructing a well-patterned constraint coefficient matrix, the solution process of OPF is accelerated. Sadat et al. [4] proposed an improved successive linear programming algorithm that significantly reduces the number of iterations needed to solve the OPF problem. The conventional methods mentioned above are centralized, sometimes some of them are not the proper choices to deal with large-scale OPF problems with thousands of variables and constraints. So the distributed approaches are developed. In [5], six distributed algorithms were studied. Magnússon et al. [6] decomposed the global OPF problem into smaller problems, which are associated with each bus of power system. Different from the centralized methods, the distributed methods reduce the computational complexity of solving the OPF problem. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence theory, machine learning algorithms and models have also been gradually introduced into the fast calculation of OPF. For example, a machine learning approach was developed to optimize the real-time analysis of OPF in [7]. The deep neural network was introduced as an optimization tool in [8].
Moreover, an effective hybrid algorithm based on supervised regression classification learning was presented in [9].

The other aspect of previous work is focused on the hardware acceleration. With the rapid development of high-performance parallel computers, parallel processing technology is applied to the calculation of OPF. A popular method is to use the hardware acceleration capability of graphical processing units (GPUs) to solve the OPF problem. In the studies of [10], the majority of the computation is loaded onto GPUs. Roberge et al. [11] presented a metaheuristic-based parallel OPF algorithm with GPUs.

Although these studies have improved the speed of OPF calculation, it is necessary to further improve the response time of online analysis in modern power system, which largely integrates renewable energy sources and power electronics. In terms of data processing and transmission, the methods mentioned above are severely limited by the data transmission delay. Specifically, the data processing mode of previous work is based on the memory-disk, which means that the input/output (I/O) bottleneck of data processing still exists. Fortunately, the development of in-memory data grid (IMDG) technology provides a new idea for solving the I/O bottleneck in massive data processing [12]. IMDG is seen as a way to process diverse and massive data. Storing the data in memory and distributing it across multiple server nodes is intended to easier to access data. Thus, in this paper, we aim to further improve the response time of OPF calculation by proposing an online analysis framework, which considers both IMDG and parallel computing. The response time is defined as the total time required for the following two processes: data import and algorithm execution. The case studies based on the IEEE baseline network show that the proposed framework can greatly improve the response time of online analysis, especially in the continuous and multi-task analysis scenario.

The next of this paper is organized as follows. The mathematical model and fast responsive framework are introduced in Section II. The simulation results and analysis are shown in Section III. Finally, the conclusion is given in Section IV.

div.head: A. Mathematical Model of OPF
div.p: The mathematical model of OPF can be formulated as an optimization problem [13]. In this section, we consider a power system with n buses collected in the set S B . S G is the set of buses with generators, and S L is the set of branches. Under the condition of satisfying the operation limits of power system, the objective of OPF in this paper is to achieve the minimum power loss, which is given by the following:
div.formula: min P loss = n i=1 |V i | n j=1 |V j |(G ij cos δ ij + B ij sin δ ij ) (1)
div.p: where P loss means the power loss, V i and V j are the voltage magnitudes of buses i and j, respectively. G ij and B ij are the conductance and susceptance between buses i and j, respectively. And δ ij is the phase difference of voltages between buses i and j.
The constraints of the proposed OPF objective are as follows:
1) Power balance: The net injected active power P i and net injected reactive power Q i at bus i are represented as:
div.formula: P i = V i n j=1 |V j |(G ij cos δ ij + B ij sin δ ij ) (i ∈ S B ) (2) Q i = V i n j=1 |V j |(G ij sin δ ij -B ij cos δ ij ) (i ∈ S B ) (3)
div.p: and they equal to the differences between generation and load at this bus:
div.formula: P i = P Gi -P Di (i ∈ S B )(4)
Q i = Q Gi -Q Di (i ∈ S B )(5)
div.p: Here, P Gi is the active power at ith generator in the generator set, and Q Gi is the reactive power at ith generator in the generator set. If there is no generator at bus i, P Gi and Q Gi are equal to zero. P Di and Q Di are the active load and reactive load at bus i, respectively.
2) Generator power and voltage magnitude limits:
div.formula: P min Gi ≤ P Gi ≤ P max Gi (i ∈ S G )(6)
Q min Gi ≤ Q Gi ≤ Q max Gi (i ∈ S G )(7)
V min i ≤ V i ≤ V max i (i ∈ S B )(8)
div.p: 3) Branch power limits:
div.formula: S min Li ≤ S Li ≤ S max Li (i ∈ S L )(9)
div.p: where S Li is the apparent power flowing through the branch i.

div.head: B. The Mechanism of In-Memory Data Grid
div.p: In the scene of massive data in power system, the transmission of data will bring great delay. Fortunately, with the introduction of in-memory computing, IMDG can avoid this delay by moving algorithms rather than data. It is also an intelligent distributed cache solution. IMDG stores data in memory and distributes it across multiple servers. If the memory is used as storage space, there will be two disadvantages: capacity and reliability. In fact, IMDG can overcome the bottleneck of memory capacity by increasing the number of server nodes. According to the actual test, the memory space occupied by 16 million grid resources is 18G [14]. In today's rapid development of computer hardware technology, it is possible to take advantage of IMDG to realize real-time OPF calculation of large-scale power system. In addition, IMDG can solve the reliability problem through the redundant backup mechanism.

As shown in Fig. 2, IMDG can be seen as a cluster composed of multiple server nodes, and it can serve as an intermediate layer between (relational database management system) RDBMS and application software (AS). Here, the data, which are temporary or need to be frequently accessed, are storaged. Different from the in-memory database (IMDB), IMDG focuses on data processing, while IMDB is about storage. IMDG can process data and perform calculation tasks in RAM. The data results in IMDG can also be sent back to the RDBMS. But IMDB cannot be applied to existing applications without transferring its datasets. Compared with the general distributed cache methods, IMDG can simplify the development of applications, and shield the interaction details between the applications and databases.

The data model in IMDG is object-oriented. Therefore, in this paper, we need to use the object-oriented approach to build the grid data model. The data objects include bus objects, branch objects and methods to obtain various attributes of the objects. Through the interfaces provided by IMDG, the objects serialized by Hash function are stored as key-value pairs to the cluster. Before the execution of calculation tasks, the data objects have been deployed in the cluster. In this case, the IMDG functions as a cached database. Then the OPF algorithm can be assigned to the nodes of the cluster for execution. By obtaining data directly from memory, the data access efficiency is improved.

div.head: A. Description of the Proposed Framework
div.p: The simulation in this paper is carried out on a computer with 8 cores, 16 threads and 16G memory. We deploy a Java-based IMDG framework in an embedded manner. The framework consists of a cluster of Java virtual machines with distributed cache and parallel computing capabilities. The cluster has the following advantages:

1) Load balance. In the server cluster, all nodes store the same amount of data, and the data share the storage space and computing resources of the entire cluster. If the number of nodes in the cluster changes, the data are automatically migrated across the cluster until it is evenly distributed.

2) Robustness. With the introduction of the mechanism of redundant backup, we can backup data and tasks among the nodes of the cluster. In this way, the cluster can effectively avoid the single fault.

3) Parallel computing. In the distributed environment built in this paper, tasks are submitted to each node of the cluster for execution, one node can obtain data from other nodes and process several tasks at the same time.
After the proposed framework is deployed, we need to verify its performance to handle actual tasks. The corresponding simulation is carried out below.

div.head: B. Parallel Computing Test
div.p: At first, we study the performance of the response time of the proposed framework to OPF calculation tasks. The simulation process is shown in Fig. 3 and described in detail as follows.

• Step 1: Original data acquisition. We can obtain the original bus data and branch data from the local database through the Java application interface. • Step 2: Modeling of original data. In this step, the power grid data model is established in an object-oriented manner. • Step 3: Import the data model. We simulate the distributed nodes of IMDG by running multiple Java virtual machines on the computer, then the serialized data model is imported into the nodes through the interface functions provided by the framework. • Step 4: Create distributed durable OPF tasks with return values. The durability means tasks on one node have backups at other nodes. In this way, if one of the nodes fails, the task on this node will continue at other nodes. • Step 5: Tasks execution. We can randomly push calculation tasks to the nodes of the cluster for execution, this means that the OPF tasks are executed in memory. • Step 6: Feedback of calculation results. The results of the OPF calculation tasks will be displayed on the computer.

The simulation data are referenced from the IEEE 57-bus system [15]. Considering the data size of the simulation data is small and the data model is only imported once into the memory, the process of importing data takes very little time. Specifically, it takes only about 0.3 seconds to import the data of the IEEE 57-bus system from the local database to the cluster's memory. So the response time is approximately equal to the execution time of the algorithm in this section. Then we observed the execution time and acceleration ratio of the framework in the multi-task scenario by increasing the number of parallel tasks.

div.head: C. Comparison of Traditional Method with the Proposed Framework
div.p: In this part, the implementation of the OPF algorithm in the traditional method and the proposed framework are compared. As shown in Table I, under a single task, the execution speed of the IMDG-based OPF program is inferior to that of the traditional method. Without any improvement on the OPF algorithm based on the interior-point method, operations such as inversion and multiplication of high-dimensional matrices are involved in the calculation process. Considering the efficient computing ability of matrix in the execution environment, most of traditional methods basically perform the OPF algorithm in the environment of MATLAB in a serial manner. In theory, MATLAB should be faster than the proposed framework for a single OPF task.

However, with the parallel computing ability, the proposed framework can avoid the defects of matrix calculation ability in the multi-task scenario. The results in Fig. 5 illustrate that in the multi-task scenario, the IMDG-based framework is more effective, and it achieves acceleration in the basic interior-point method. The proposed framework has the advantage of executing distributed parallel tasks, which can realize the simultaneous calculation of the power flow in multiple regions.

div.head: IV. CONCLUSION
div.p: The main purpose of this paper is to improve the response time of online analysis in power system. Specifically, a fast responsive framework, which considers the distributed cache and in-memory computing of IMDG, for OPF analysis is proposed. The results show that the proposed framework can greatly improve the response time in dealing with the real-time calculation of the mult-task scenario. If advanced algorithms and high-performance servers are adopted, the proposed framework can be further improved. Moreover, this framework has broad potential application in other online analysis scenarios which require real-time and parallel processing, and provides a useful insight for safe and stable operation in power system.
